To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have used cell type- specific markers to identify and characterize the major neural cell types in human fetal brain cell cultures.

(a) the major cell classes in human fetal nervous tissue cultures are glial cells, neurons, and leptomeninges cells; (b) astrocytes can be distinguished from oligodendroglial and Schwann cells on the basis of their expression of the intermediate filament protein GFAP; (c) oligodendroblasts can be distinguished from Schwann cells by their expression of the cell surface glycolipid galactocerebroside; (d)
the markers used in this study can identify astrocytes, oligodendroytes, neurons, macrophages (microglia), leptomeningeals, and fibroblasts in human neural cell cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development, maintenance and regeneration of the central and peripheral nervous system in man, with emphasis on glial cells and their role in myelination and axonal support.
the identification and characterization of the major classes of cells present in dissociated cultures of human nervous system tissue.
the development of cell type-specific markers and their application to the analysis of neural cells in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cell type-specific markers we have used are useful to identify and study astrocytes, oligodendrogliocytes, and macrophage-like cells in culture, but that their usefulness to identify and characterize neurons is limited.
these cell type-specific markers can be used to identify and characterize the major classes of cells in dissociated cultures of human fetal brain and spinal cord.
the markers used here are not specific for any one cell type in the nervous system, but are useful for identifying and studying specific populations of cells in culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the markers for astrocytes, oligodendocytes, and neurons in human fetal neural tissue in vitro are very similar to those of their counterparts in rodent neural tissue.
the major classes of glial and neuronal cell types in human fetal nervous tissue are readily identified and studied in culture using the markers described above.
astrocytes are the most numerous cell class in the cultures and that they express Thy-1, fibronectin, and the glial fibrillary protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain and study pure cell populations from human fetal neural tissue, and that this approach should prove valuable in the study of human neural development, disease, and aging.

it is possible to identify, in culture, the major types of cells that make up the central nervous system and to use them for studying the interactions among different cell types and between the cells and their environment.
cell type-specific markers can be identified and used to study the development and properties of the various classes of neural cells.
